envelope.text: There is no goal handle here: the call is on the SERVER, keyed by goal id,

why:
publishes a feedback message for one live goal. rclcpp_action spells it `ServerGoalHandle::publish_feedback(shared_ptr<Feedback>)` -- a method on the owning handle its accepted callback was given. Ours is on the SERVER and keyed by goal id, because with no allocator the goals live in a static arena the server owns rather than in a handle handed to the application (the constraint `rust:ActionClient::wait_for_action_server` records for the typestate chain). Takes the feedback by const reference, not by `shared_ptr`.

phase-428 (RFC-0089): re-keyed by the namespace flip. `nros::ActionClient<A>` / `nros::ActionServer<A>` are now aliases of `rclcpp_action::Client<A>` / `rclcpp_action::Server<A>`, which the extractor keys as `Client::*` / `Server::*`. The type is `same` now and the member is `ours-only`, so it no longer inherits its type's verdict and carries its own.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ENVELOPE WRITTEN where a porting user reads it: the method's doc comment states the server-side, goal-id-keyed, const-reference shape against upstream's `goal_handle->publish_feedback(std::shared_ptr<Feedback>)`.
